title: Switchbot BlindTilt Light Level Stuck
body:
### The problem

I installed my first Switchbot BlindTilt two weeks ago and the Light Level has been stuck at 2 for the entirety of the time.  The battery level is updating and my automation to open/close it is working just fine.

I have found in the logs some messages about it not being connected (see below), but otherwise everything else is still functional.  The SwitchBot app also shows the light level just fine.

I also found this issue reported in not this repo: https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant.io/issues/27464

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2023.5.4

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

SwitchBot

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/switchbot/

### Diagnostics information

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Same here, I have 7 installed. 6 stuck at 2 and 1 that I saw at 1 when I first installed it, unfortunately, I disabled the light entity on it right after since it's useless, so I don't know if it would have got to 2 then stopped. 
All 7 running FW 2.0.0

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: Thought I was the only one who noticed this but glad to see it's already a documented issue.

comments.author: participant3
comments.body: I am wondering if this is because of the latest firmware update....Is everything pulled from API or a Bluetooth connection?

comments.author: participant4
comments.body:
If I remember correctly there use to be 2 lux sensors, one in the wand and another in the solar panel. The official app used to give us the option to use the internal or solar sensors. But soon after updates this option is gone. 
I've disconnected the solar panel in hope it would use the internal sensor and still getting a reading of 2 in HA but in the app I says panel disconnected and it will run the automation set in the app (if level falls below 2, close blind)

Another observation is the charging function in the app, it supposed to only charge when at level 6 or above. In my case I'm experiencing some of my devices will charge from level 4 and others only from 6 and above.

I genuinely think the firmware is a little clunky still or there's been hardware issues and switchbot is trying to fix things with gimmicks so kinda feel sorry for the devs here trying to make sense of it all.

I'm not getting any errors in the logs atm but hope any of the above is of any helpfulness.

comments.author: participant5
comments.body:
Same issue here with 7 blind tilt units. Light level reporting by HA is 2 or 1. But in the Switchbot App it reports 1-10. This issue seems to be how the intergration is getting (or not getting) the light level information and reporting it. All batteries are charging when the sun is on solar panels.
REF: same with Switchbot versions 2.0 and 2.1. Have the latest updates of if this date available in HA.

comments.author: participant8
comments.body:
I've sent them an email to see if I get a different response!

> I hope this email find you well on a spooky Halloween!

> Last year I bought 5 Switchbot Blind Tilt devices for use in my home. I have used the Bluetooth connection to control them all using [an integration in home assistant](https://www.participant22.io/integrations/switchbot/). This integration has worked wonderfully for me for this past year on all of my devices, despite knowing that it is not support by Switchbot and is community made.

> My question for you all stems from [this conversation on GitHub](https://github.com/participant22/core/issues/94742) that has been an ongoing issue for me this past year. I am hoping that someone from your development team is able to take the time to read through this brief issue. Essentially, as far as we can tell, the light level sensed from each device constantly reports either a 1 or more commonly 2.

> It is completely possible that we are [interpreting the Bluetooth variables incorrectly](https://github.com/participant22/core/blob/45ff4940eb85b76f37dce118c9af9e8449afc55c/homeassistant/components/switchbot/sensor.py#L62). If so, could you give us some basic direction on how we could achieve this?

> Thank you for any help you can provide! This integration is what led me to buy devices from you in the first place!

comments.author: participant8
comments.body:
I was redirected to https://github.com/OpenWonderLabs/SwitchBotAPI?tab=readme-ov-file#blind-tilt.

I don't see anything mentioning light level in that api, but I am also thinking that this is the cloud api and not the local bluetooth one. [This person still asked about it last week though.](https://github.com/OpenWonderLabs/SwitchBotAPI/issues/356)

Would someone smarter than me be able to weigh in? Would it be worthwhile to create an issue about the Bluetooth api and this specific issue, and then ask for forgiveness if it ever gets attention?

comments.author: participant8
comments.body:
Yeah, the vibe I got looking at the cloud api before was that this value is not exposed over bluetooth anyways. You aren't even able to make more than 2-3 automations based on the light level in the app with a hub, since those automations run locally on the device.

I started using integrations like https://github.com/basbruss/adaptive-cover, but now I am more leaning to just using my temperature sensor outside to detect direct sunlight (yellow below) since I have been having reliability issues with that integration. 
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/92103e32-d30e-4256-a2a7-73eec3794a1e)


@participant7 have you ever had issues with the blinds closing, then blocking enough light for them to reopen, just to close again? I'd be interested to see how you implemented that, since I do have a similar light sensor.

I was hoping I could get something much more usable with HA...

> Hey guys, I have fixed this issue. Please refer to PR [sblibs/pySwitchbot#342](https://github.com/sblibs/pySwitchbot/pull/342) and [#145360](https://github.com/participant22/core/pull/145360) . You can update pyswitchbot to version 0.64.1 to solve this issue, or wait for the official version release.

Excellent! I hope I speak on behalf of those who appreciate listening to and being responsive to customer feedback. And thank you for supporting the efforts of open-source projects such as Home Assistant.... I know I for one will factor that into my decision to purchase SwitchBot products in the future as well as recommend them to others.

Appreciate your help and responsiveness.
